key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 perovskites strongly tunes bandgap and solar efficiency, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the best photovoltaic candidate.
engineering_relevance: This provides a compositional design rule for engineering perovskite materials with targeted absorption and efficiency for solar-cell applications.
method: First-principles calculations of structural, electronic, and optical properties
Band structure analysis to determine bandgap type and range
SLME screening to estimate solar-cell efficiency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps from 2.0 to 3.788 eV and SLME values ranging from 0.6% for Ca3PF3 to 29.6% for Ca3PI3.
watch_item: The results are computational screening outputs, so experimental stability, defect effects, and device-level fabrication constraints still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
